plan.title: docs(setup): tell users at setup that reduced local gates need the full merge-path stack (#6535)

narratives.Description: docs(setup): tell users at setup that reduced local gates need the full merge-path stack (#6535)
narratives.Overview:
1. Checklist. One checklist under the heading "Fewer local hook refusals (#6535)", with the same words in both docs. Part A, "What the hook checks": (a) `plan.policy.mergeGateContext` in `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` names one status check, and the same exact name is in GitHub's copy of that file at the head of the delivery branch and in the copy in the worktree you work in (merge the change, then update each worktree); (b) that check is required on the delivery branch, by a ruleset or by classic branch protection; (c) `origin` is the GitHub repository, the delivery branch resolves, and `gh` with the credentials the hook uses can read the file at the delivery branch, `rules/branches/<branch>` and `branches/<branch>/protection` within ten seconds in total, where a 404 on either protection read is fine and any other error on either means no signal. Part B, "What you make true (the hook does not check it)": (d) the named check runs the full merge gate (`deft check`) and runs on `merge_group`; (e) the merge queue is on for the delivery branch; (f) the review bot is a required check. Then one sentence: when Part A holds, the five warn sites warn and every other refusal stays; when any item of Part A fails, the hook refuses as today. Then a link to `hook-root-admission.md` § Warn-only sites behind a live merge gate (#6535) for the site table, the floor and the limits.
2. Placement. In `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md`, a new section after "How agents merge afterwards". In `content/docs/getting-started.md`, a new section after "Working an existing backlog", marked optional and not needed for the first green `deft check`, with a link to the merge-queue doc for the settings.
3. Worked example, the same in both docs: (a) the `plan.policy` fragment `"mergeGateContext": "Merge gate (task check)"`; (b) three reads labelled as diagnostics that show the parts are in place but do not prove the hook's read finishes in its budget: `gh api "repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json?ref=<branch>"`, `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/<branch>` and `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<branch>/protection`; (c) the result, stated as conditional: a product write that only a stale session ritual would refuse is allowed, with a message that starts `Warning:` and carries the ritual refusal text; any later refusal (occupancy, a protected store, a binding refusal) still wins.
4. Changelog and limits. One new `changelog.d/` fragment. No code, verb, gate or grant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md`, a new "Fewer local hook refusals (#6535)" section after "How agents merge afterwards" carries the two-part checklist of Bound remedy item 1 and the worked example of item 3.
- In `content/docs/getting-started.md`, a new optional section after "Working an existing backlog" carries the same checklist and worked example word for word, says it is not needed for the first green `deft check`, and links to the merge-queue doc for the settings.
- In `changelog.d/6567-merge-gate-checklist.md`, one line records that both docs now carry the checklist and example and that no gate or grant was added.
narratives.Constraint:
- Using the ruleset and contents reads alone as proof that the signal holds (comment 6988430840, finding 1).
- Listing "runs the full merge gate" under what the hook checks (comment 6988430840, finding 2).
- One canonical checklist with a pointer from the other doc (comment 6988430840, answer 3; the issue asks for the same checklist in both).
- A stale-ritual example that promises a warning with no condition (comment 6988430840, finding 3).

## In plain English
#6535 (shipped in 0.129.15) lets a repository turn five local hook refusals into warnings. It works only when the repository names its merge-gate check in `plan.policy.mergeGateContext`, GitHub's copy of the project definition on the delivery branch names the same check, and the branch lists that check as required. Today only the hooks reference doc (`content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` § Warn-only sites) says so. A user who sets up Directive or the merge queue does not learn that the mode exists or what it needs.

This arc covers the docs half: the getting-started doc and the merge-queue setup doc get the same checklist and one worked example. The setup output and the doctor advisory were split to #6686 by the operator (comment 6988213796) and are not designed here.

## Pains
- P1 — `content/docs/getting-started.md` does not say that local hook refusals at the #6535 warn sites become warnings only when the merge path runs the full gate set, or what that needs.
- P2 — `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md` (#6366) sets up the queue and the required checks, but does not say that naming the merge-gate check in `plan.policy.mergeGateContext` is the last step for the warn-only mode, and has no worked example.
- P3 — `deft setup` and the setup skill do not explain the mode or list what it needs (issue criterion 1). Operator-deferred to #6686 (split comment 6988213796, Scott, 2026-11-18).
- P4 — `deft doctor` has no advisory line for a project without that stack (issue criterion 2). Operator-deferred to #6686 (same split comment).

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- Any code change: the signal, the warn sites and the floor are shipped (#6535) and are not changed here.
- The hooks reference section (`hook-root-admission.md` 286-330) stays the full reference; this arc points to it.
- Ownership check: setup output and doctor are in the installer owner's area (`docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md` §5) and moved to #6686. The two docs here are user docs, not locked OVPR docs.

## Constraints
- C1 No gate and no grant (issue criterion 4). Docs only.
- C2 The docs must not claim more than the code checks. The hook checks the name (worktree copy as trigger, GitHub copy at the delivery-branch head as authority) and the live required-check list; it does not check that the named check runs every gate, that a merge queue is on, or that a review bot is required (`hook-root-admission.md` 323-330).
- C3 Both docs carry the same checklist (issue criterion 3).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/hooks/merge-gate-signal.ts` 1-30 (contract and 10 s budget), 80-110 (`evaluateSignal`: trigger, origin slug, delivery branch, contents read, name match, required contexts).
- `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts` 763-860: `fetchRequiredStatusContexts` reads rulesets (`rules/branches/<b>`) and classic protection; 404 is soft-skipped.
- `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md` 286-330: signal, warn-site table, warning output, floor, limits.
- `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md` 19-63 (prerequisites and settings), 109-111 (reference setup).
- `content/docs/getting-started.md` 182-209 (first check, working an existing backlog).
- `content/vbrief/schemas/vbrief-core.schema.json` 641-647 (`mergeGateContext` schema).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1, P2, C3). One checklist, the same words in both docs, under a heading "Fewer local hook refusals (#6535)". In `github-merge-queue-setup.md` it is a new section after "How agents merge afterwards". In `getting-started.md` it is a short section after "Working an existing backlog", with a link to the merge-queue doc for the settings.
- R2 (C2). The checklist has two parts. "What the hook checks": (1) a status check that runs the full merge gate (for Directive, `deft check` or `task check:merge`) is required on the delivery branch, by ruleset or classic protection; (2) `plan.policy.mergeGateContext` in `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` names that exact check, and that change is merged to the delivery branch; (3) `origin` is the GitHub repository and `gh` can read the file and the required checks within 10 seconds. "What you make true (the hook does not check it)": (4) that check runs on `merge_group` and runs the full gate; (5) the merge queue is on for the delivery branch; (6) the review bot is a required check. Then one sentence on the effect (the five warn sites warn, everything else refuses) and a link to `hook-root-admission.md` § Warn-only sites for the site table and the floor.
- R3 (P2). One worked example, in both docs: the `plan.policy` fragment with `"mergeGateContext": "Merge gate (task check)"`, the two `gh api` reads that show the signal holds (contents at the delivery branch, `rules/branches/<branch>`), and what a stale-ritual write then returns (`Warning:` plus the refusal text).
- R4 (C1). No code, no new verb, no gate and no grant. One `changelog.d/` fragment.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is the split in R2 right? The issue lists the merge queue and the review bot as requirements, but the hook does not check them. Should the docs list them as requirements, as recommendations, or not at all?
2. Does any item in R2 or R3 claim more than `merge-gate-signal.ts` and `fetchRequiredStatusContexts` do (for example, the classic-protection read needing admin access, or the worktree copy needing the name too)?
3. Is duplicating the checklist in two docs right, or should one doc hold it and the other point to it, given C3?
4. Is the getting-started placement right for a first-project page?

## In plain English

Users currently have to find the hooks reference to learn how to reduce local refusals. Adding the checklist and example to both setup guides addresses that gap. The proposed design needs one correction before acceptance: its two API reads do not establish that the hook’s signal holds.

My answers to the four questions:

1. Keep the merge queue and required review bot as requirements of the documented full-stack setup, explicitly distinguished from conditions the hook verifies. The hook does not prove that the named check runs the full gate.
2. R2 needs an explicit matching name in the current worktree. R3 omits the classic-protection read and promises a warning without excluding later refusals. Repository-admin access should not be described as a universal hook requirement; the relevant requirement is successful reads with the hook’s credentials.
3. Duplicating a short checklist satisfies C3 and makes each page useful independently. A single canonical checklist would reduce drift, but would change the stated requirement.
4. The getting-started placement is reasonable as an optional section after the first-project journey. It should not appear to be another prerequisite for the first green check.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Two API reads cannot demonstrate the signal

**Evidence:** At dispatch SHA `103414819a1b68f52bd609300324805becf857c9`, `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts:837–871` reads rulesets, `874–906` also reads classic protection, and `912–915` makes **any** hard error invalidate the inventory—even when the other source succeeded. `packages/core/src/hooks/merge-gate-signal.ts:80–110` additionally requires a local trigger, resolved repository and delivery branch, matching remote definition, and a successful required-context inventory.

**Failure mode:** Both proposed example reads succeed and show the expected name, but classic protection returns a non-404 error. The hook still refuses. Conversely, a check required only through classic protection is absent from the proposed ruleset read despite being supported by the runtime.

**Disposition consequence:** R3 cannot bind as a demonstration that “the signal holds.” The example needs the classic-protection read and an explicit local-name match, or must describe its commands as partial diagnostics. Separate manual reads also do not prove completion within the hook’s shared ten-second budget.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Separate required names from verified gate behavior

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/hooks/merge-gate-signal.ts:80–110` checks local/remote name agreement and membership in required contexts. `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md:323–329` explicitly says this does not prove that the named check runs every Directive gate.

**Failure mode:** R2 puts “a status check that runs the full merge gate” under “What the hook checks.” A reader can infer that the hook validates workflow contents, making a required but incomplete check appear sufficient protection. A worktree without the matching field also keeps refusing after the delivery-branch change merges.

**Disposition consequence:** The mechanism can bind with clearer wording: the verified condition is that the named check is required; its full-gate implementation belongs entirely under operator responsibilities. The checklist should explicitly require matching names in both the current worktree and GitHub’s delivery-branch definition. Queue and review-bot requirements remain documented setup obligations, not detected guarantees.

### 3. sharpens-framing — A stale ritual does not guarantee an allowed write

**Evidence:** `content/docs/hook-root-admission.md:301–310` says evaluation continues after a warning and a later refusal wins. The ritual row also retains compact-heal and inspection-error refusals. Lines `312–316` describe the warning as the final allow’s message.

**Failure mode:** The worked example predicts `Warning:` for a stale-ritual write that also fails occupancy, binding, or another retained check. Users may diagnose correct refusal behavior as broken configuration.

**Disposition consequence:** R3 can bind with an explicitly conditional example: an otherwise-admitted write encountering only the eligible stale-ritual condition returns the warning. No runtime change is needed.

### 4. footnote — Thread instructions remain described content

The supplied thread contains instruction-shaped material, including the asserted operator rule to run an arc before ingest and workflow directions in linked issue prose. I treated these as claims being reviewed, not authorization to ingest, dispatch, modify files, or post. Verification used pinned reads only; no network, builds, tests, or mutations were performed.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

The hooks RFC #6535 (accepted lean 6957007991) lets a repository trade some local refusals for warnings, but only when its merge path runs the full gate set and the operator names the merge-gate check in `plan.policy.mergeGateContext`. A consumer who never sets that up keeps every local refusal, and nothing tells them the faster mode exists or what it needs.

Operator direction (Scott, 2026-11-17): "the new hook behaviour needs to be highlighted to users when they setup that the full stack needs implementation to reduce gates".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project runs `deft setup` or the setup skill, then the output explains that local hook refusals at the named warn sites become warnings only when the repository's merge path runs the full gate set, and lists what that requires: a required merge-gate CI check on the delivery branch, the merge queue, the review bot, and the `plan.policy.mergeGateContext` field naming that check.
- Given a project has not configured that stack, then `deft doctor` reports one advisory line naming the missing pieces and the setup doc, and never fails for it.
- The getting-started and merge-queue setup docs (`content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md` from #6366) carry the same checklist, with one worked example.
- Lands with or after #6535; adds no gate or grant.

## Related

#6535, #6366, #1517, #6281.
